purpose: Summative performance task for the full unit. Each child picks a rule (single-step or multi-step), builds an animal parade, translates to a number parade with whole numbers up to 1000, organizes as a table of values, predicts term 50, justifies formally, and states a generalization. Used as primary summative evidence for C1.1, C1.2, C1.3, and C1.4.
student_learning_goal: I can build a number parade up to 1000, organize it as a table of values, predict term 50, and justify my rule.

parts.answer_key: An 8-cell parade following the rule the child wrote, with a matching 8-term number sequence where all values are between 0 and 1000. Examples: Rule +75 starting at 75 → 75, 150, 225, 300, 375, 450, 525, 600. Rule ×2 starting at 5 → 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640. Rule -50 starting at 800 → 800, 750, 700, 650, 600, 550, 500, 450. Multi-step rule '+30 then -10' starting at 100 → 100, 130, 120, 150, 140, 170, 160, 190. Correct if the rule is preserved AND all values 0-1000 inclusive.

parts.answer_key: Value column: copies the 8 numbers from Part 2 in matching term order. Term 50 prediction: depends on the rule. For +75 starting at 75, term 50 = 50 × 75 = 3750 — over 1000, so the answer is 'OFF THE CHART; my parade reaches 1000 at term 13 (since 13 × 75 = 975 and 14 × 75 = 1050).' For ×2 starting at 5, term 50 = 5 × 2^49 (astronomically large) — 'OFF THE CHART; values exceed 1000 at term 8 since 5 × 2^7 = 640 and 5 × 2^8 = 1280.' For -50 starting at 800, term 50 doesn't make sense because the parade ends at term 17 (negative thereafter). For multi-step, more complex reasoning. JUSTIFY sentence must include start, rule, jumps, and result. GENERALIZATION: any reasonable formula or description connecting term K to value (e.g., 'value = K × 75' for +N rules starting at N).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, try the same exercise with a DIFFERENT rule type. If you did growing, try shrinking. If you did single-step, try multi-step. Build the new parade, table, and term-50 prediction.
teacher_notes: SUMMATIVE worksheet — the most important artifact in the unit. Score each completed worksheet against the 4-level rubric (see assessment_suite). Look for: (1) Did rule, type, and core/terms align in Part 1? — C1.3 evidence. (2) Did the 8 animal cells follow the rule AND did number cells stay 0-1000? — C1.1 + C1.4 evidence. (3) Did the table use correct headers AND match Part 2? — C1.2 evidence. (4) Did term-50 prediction use multiplication shortcut (not drawing)? — C1.3 + C1.4 capstone. (5) Did justification sentence reference rule AND number of jumps? — C1.3 deepest evidence. (6) Did generalization express a relationship (e.g., 'value = K × N')? — L4 evidence. Children at L4 on every dimension are ready for Grade 4.
